blurb: Smallest AKC sporting dog, known for its domed head and silky feathered coat
description: The American Cocker Spaniel is a small US sporting spaniel with a domed head, long ears and a silky feathered coat, known for its merry, even temper.
answer: The American Cocker Spaniel is a small sporting spaniel from the United States that diverged from the English Cocker Spaniel during the 20th century. It stands about 34 to 39 cm tall, typically weighs around 11 to 14 kg, and is known as the Merry Cocker for its even, people-oriented temperament.

body: Spaniels came to North America as early as the Mayflower in 1620, and the first Cocker Spaniel was registered with the American Kennel Club in 1878. The American Spaniel Club, founded in 1881, is the oldest breed club in the United States. The modern breed traces back to Ch. Obo II, whose sire was considered the father of the English Cocker.

Differing US and UK standards drove the two types apart by the 1920s, and the AKC recognised the English Cocker as a separate breed in 1946; the UK Kennel Club followed in 1970. The American Cocker was the most popular US breed for a total of 18 years, has won Best in Show at Westminster four times and won at Crufts in 2017.

It is the smallest sporting breed recognised by the AKC. The head is immediately recognisable, with a rounded dome, a pronounced stop, a square lip and large, round dark eyes. Long, low-set ears and medium-long silky fur with feathering on the legs and belly are typical. Colours fall into black or black and tan, any solid colour other than black (ASCOB), and parti-colour.

The breed standard calls for a dog that is equable in temperament with no suggestion of timidity. With early socialisation it is said to live well with adults, children and other pets, and it generally prefers regular human company to isolation. Some individuals may be sensitive to loud noises or rough handling. Breeding for the show ring has made it less suited to field work.
Sources give little specific exercise guidance. The long, silky show coat and long ears are generally expected to need regular grooming and attention.

One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years. Conditions reported in the breed include progressive rod-cone degeneration, glaucoma, a taurine-related form of dilated cardiomyopathy, hypothyroidism, otitis externa and several skin conditions such as allergic skin disease and Malassezia dermatitis. One US study found glaucoma in 5.52% of dogs, the highest prevalence of any breed, while hip dysplasia was less common than average.

faq.q: How big does an American Cocker Spaniel get?
faq.a: It stands about 34 to 39 cm at the withers and usually weighs around 11 to 14 kg, with females slightly lighter.

faq.q: How long do American Cocker Spaniels live?
faq.a: Typical lifespan is about 10 to 14 years; one 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between American and English Cocker Spaniels?
faq.a: The American Cocker is smaller, with a rounder domed skull, rounder eyes and a shorter muzzle, while the English Cocker is slightly larger with a more setter-like head.
